name: Jupiter
overview: Scripture references Jupiter as a prominent Greek and Roman deity, highlighting the cultural context in which early Christians ministered. In Acts 14, Barnabas is called Jupiter by the people, reflecting their association of him with the chief god, and the local priest of Jupiter attempts to lead a sacrifice, illustrating the idolatrous practices prevalent in that era. Additionally, Acts 19 mentions an image that fell from Jupiter, indicating the tangible presence of this pagan worship in cities like Ephesus. These passages underscore the challenge of proclaiming Christ in a world steeped in false gods and idolatry.
